description: Wil je meebouwen aan de zorg van morgen met AI? Als stagiair bij Pacmed bouw je modellen die de besluitvorming in Nederlandse ziekenhuizen elke dag verbeteren. Je werkt met echte klinische data, samen met data scientists, engineers en clinici. We zoeken twee stagiairs die starten tussen december 2026 en maart 2027. Over Pacmed Bij Pacmed combineren we technologie en menselijkheid om de zorg toegankelijk en toekomstbestendig te houden. Onze software draait al in meerdere Nederlandse ziekenhuizen en we breiden actief verder uit. We helpen zorgprofessionals om real-time betere beslissingen te nemen, capaciteit efficiënter te benutten en patiëntenstromen soepel te laten verlopen. Als stagiair zit je precies op het punt waar onze modellen en data de klinische praktijk raken. Waarom Pacmed een ideale stageplek is: We zijn een scale-up met een duidelijke missie: de zorg toegankelijk en toekomstbestendig houden. Je werk doet ertoe. Het komt terecht in producten die in ziekenhuizen gebruikt worden, niet in een la. Je krijgt een begeleider die investeert in je ontwikkeling, en een team dat elkaar graag beter maakt. We gaan vriendelijk en respectvol met elkaar om en hebben graag plezier, met regelmatige teamuitjes en een jaarlijkse off-site. De twee stages Elke stagiair krijgt een eigen project. Beide projecten gaan over patiëntenstromen: hoeveel patiënten komen het ziekenhuis binnen, en hoeveel stromen er uit naar de nazorg. Stage 1: instroom voorspellen op de acute as (Capaciteitsmonitor) De Pacmed Capaciteitsmonitor geeft zorgprofessionals AI-voorspellingen op basis van real-time ziekenhuisdata, zodat ze personeel en capaciteit proactief kunnen plannen in plaats van reactief. De capaciteitsmonitor voorspelt patiëntbezetting en zorgzwaarte en vertaalt dat naar de daadwerkelijk benodigde personele capaciteit. We breiden deze aanpak nu uit naar andere afdelingen op de acute as: de spoedeisende hulp (SEH), de eerste harthulp (EHH) en de cardiac care unit (CCU). Daar houdt de personeelsplanning nog weinig rekening met schommelingen in de instroom, met over- en onderbezetting als gevolg. Sinds september 2026 werkt een stagiair aan instroommodellen voor deze afdelingen. Jij versterkt dat project en bouwt erop voort. Denk aan: modellen voor de SEH, EHH en CCU ontwikkelen en verbeteren op basis van ziekenhuisdata over instroom, uitstroom en bezetting en publieke data zoals weer, evenementen en epidemiologische gegevens de (potentiële) impact van de AI modellen op de personeelsplanning doorrekenen afdelingen (SEH, EHH, CCU) of ziekenhuizen met elkaar vergelijken; de uitkomsten samen met clinici interpreteren en valideren. Stage 2: uitstroom naar de VVT voorspellen (Transfer Monitor) De Pacmed Transfer Monitor richt zich op een van de grotere inefficiënties in Nederlandse ziekenhuizen: vertraagde overplaatsing van patiënten naar de nazorg. Patiënten die medisch gezien niet meer in het ziekenhuis hoeven te liggen maar nog nergens terechtkunnen ("verkeerde bedden") zijn naar schatting goed voor 5 tot 15% van de ligdagen in de ziekenhuizen waarmee we werken. Dat blokkeert de doorstroom vanaf bijvoorbeeld de SEH en het electieve programma, is vervelend voor patiënten, verhoogt het risico op complicaties en kost onnodig geld. De Transfer Monitor voorspelt vroeg en per patiënt of iemand nazorg nodig heeft en wat de verwachte ontslagdatum is. Zo kan het transferbureau bepalen welke patiënten het eerst gescreend worden, en kunnen artsen en verpleegkundigen het ontslag op tijd regelen. In deze stage gebruik je klinische data om te voorspellen hoeveel patiënten uitstromen naar VVT-instellingen (verpleeg- en verzorgingshuizen en thuiszorg). Daarmee kunnen die instellingen hun eigen capaciteit beter plannen. Je bouwt en evalueert het model en toetst het samen met ziekenhuizen en nazorginstellingen. Wat ga je doen? Je traint en evalueert machine-learningmodellen op echte ziekenhuisdata. Je ontwerpt en voert impactanalyses uit die de klinische waarde van onze producten laten zien en verbeteren. Je schuift aan bij sessies met clinici om hun werkproces te begrijpen en dat te vertalen naar modelkeuzes. Wat bieden we Je krijgt intensieve begeleiding van een ervaren data scientist, met echte ruimte om je project zelf te trekken. Je bouwt een stevig portfolioproject op een echt clinical-AI-probleem, en de stage richten we zo in dat hij past bij de eisen van je scriptie of opleiding. Vanaf dag één hoor je er volwaardig bij. Eerdere stagiairs leverden werk op dat direct in onze producten terechtkwam, zoals ons zorgzwaartemodel. Daarnaast: een stagevergoeding van €500 per maand; regelmatige sociale activiteiten, met kwartaaluitjes en een jaarlijkse off-site; flexibele werktijden en de mogelijkheid om af en toe vanuit het buitenland te werken; 25 vakantiedagen per jaar op basis van een fulltime dienstverband (naar rato bij parttime); dagelijks lunch op kantoor, met veel vegetarische en veganistische opties; de mogelijkheid om standaard feestdagen te ruilen voor andere dagen, bijvoorbeeld voor persoonlijke of religieuze feestdagen; een laptop van de zaak voor de duur van je stage. Solliciteren De sollicitatie bestaat uit een of twee gesprekken waarbij we kennis maken, jij de kans krijgt om je vragen te stellen en wij graag meer horen over je motivatie en ervaring. Interesse? Stuur ons een korte motivatie en je cv. Vermeld je opleiding, je beschikbaarheid (startdatum en aantal uur per week) en of je een voorkeur hebt voor stage 1 of stage 2. Wie zoeken we We zoeken iemand die analyses kan uitvoeren, modellen kan bouwen en de uitkomsten hervan op een begrijpelijke manier kan presenteren en bespreken met clinici zonder data-achtergrond. Dit vragen we: Je spreekt Nederlands. Je werkt met personeelsplanners, verpleegkundig teamleiders, capaciteits- en transfermedewerkers in Nederlandse ziekenhuizen, en met Nederlandstalige data. title: Alliance Partner Manager (SaaS) | Luma
description:
Our Why At Dotmatics 

At Dotmatics, a Siemens company,  we believe science, data, and decision-making must be deeply intertwined for innovation to thrive. Our Portfolio includes Luma, LumaLab Connect, ELN Platform, Graphpad Prism, Geneious, SnapGene, Protein Metrics, OMIQ, FCS Express, LabArchives, NQuery, EasyPanel, SoftGenetics and Virscidian.

We have a vision for a new Lab of the Future that will change the future of scientific research.

We have created the world’s most comprehensive digital science platform – best-of-breed software applications already used by more than 2 million scientists, together in a single ecosystem united by a powerful, flexible enterprise data platform. This is not flat data buried away in digital graveyards. This is dynamic, multi-dimensional decision-making.

Scientific enterprises need a new level of effectiveness to achieve tomorrow’s breakthroughs. Illness will not wait. The biosphere will not wait. We are tireless in our vision, because the time for innovation is now.

Shaping the Future of Science At Dotmatics 

Our global team of more than 800 colleagues are dedicated to supporting our customers in over 180 countries. Together, with our scientific community of users, we accelerate scientific innovation in order to make the world a healthier, cleaner, and safer place to live.

You’ll join a collaborative, global team pushing the boundaries of scientific innovation.  Your ideas and efforts will have a tangible impact, accelerating scientific progress and discovery. We offer a dynamic, remote-friendly environment that fosters high integrity and collaboration, empowering you to excel. Dotmatics is a company built by scientists, for scientists. Combined, we are now the world’s largest cloud-based scientific research R&D platform. We need your help to keep growing and pioneering the future.

We are Science Driven. We are Customer Centric. We are Better Together. 

What do we need

We are seeking an Alliance Partner Manager to lead the technical dimension of our alliances and partnering function for Luma, our AI-Native Multimodal Research Platform for Scientific Intelligence. Sitting at the intersection of business and engineering, you'll own how our platform connects with, integrates into, and creates value alongside the products of our strategic technology partners, such as Databricks and AWS.

This position is based in EMEA, working globally across time zones. It is a senior role with broad scope, where you'll act as the bridge between partner engineering teams and our own product, engineering and commercial organizations, working closely with Sales, Legal, Marketing, Engineering, Product, Support and Pre-Sales, as well as colleagues at Siemens, with room to design and build the technical alliance capability around you.

While the focus is strategic, this remains a hands-on role: you'll need enough technical depth to scope integrations credibly, validate them in sandboxes, and hold your own in a conversation with a partner's engineering team. We're looking for someone with an engineering-minded, "application scientist" type approach — comfortable understanding the technical requirements involved in onboarding a partner, and operating confidently within a large company mindset and environment.

In this role you will get to:

  • Define, build, and execute the technical partner strategy, prioritising which integrations and joint solutions to build, developing and implementing joint go-to-market plans (co-sell, co-build, co-deliver), aligning teams and facilitating sales enablement and training of partners.
  • Own engineering level relationships across partner organisations through effective communication, structured governance and business reviews, and joint business planning.
  • Scope integration feasibility early in partner conversations, translating vague partner asks into clear, buildable technical specifications and setting realistic expectations.
  • Oversee solution architecture, use-case mapping, partner product certification and sandbox / proof-of-concept development to design and validate joint solutions.
  • Engage partners to develop differentiated solutions through joint collaboration, market and competitive analysis, and the creation of joint marketing collateral.
  • Evangelise partnerships internally, working closely with Sales, Legal, Marketing, Engineering, Product, Support and Pre-Sales stakeholders, and with colleagues at Siemens, feeding partner needs into the roadmap and organising collaborative events.
  • Define, track and analyse key partnership metrics, collaborating with partners to optimise performance, and represent Dotmatics/Siemens at alliance and partner conferences and events.
  • Focus specifically on systems integration partners, bringing on partners that will meaningfully increase the bottom line.

We are looking for candidate's who have 7+ years in technology partnerships, alliances, solution architecture or pre-sales engineering, including several years leading strategic technical partner or ISV relationships at enterprise scale. You've built integrations, not just managed them, and you can move fluently between a business review and a whiteboard session with a partner's engineers. You're comfortable operating with a high degree of autonomy on complex, ambiguous pursuits, and you set realistic expectations that engineering can actually deliver on.

Just as importantly, you lead through influence. You can align engineering, marketing and sales teams, internally and across partner organisations, behind a shared plan without direct authority, and you're motivated by building a partnering function and team, not just running one. While not a traditional "sales" person, you're comfortable navigating sales-style conversations, combining technical knowledge with strong relationship management and communication skills.

Given the scientific focus of the Luma platform, experience in scientific software, life sciences, pharmaceuticals, biotechnology or research-focused technology would be particularly valuable. We're interested in candidates who understand the challenges of scientific research, including scientific data, laboratory workflows and the technology platforms that support R&D.

Key Skills:

  • Technical partnership leadership - a proven track record defining and executing partner or alliance strategy with ISVs, technology platforms or system integrators, with measurable partner-sourced or partner-influenced revenue impact.
  • Hands-on integration fluency, including practical depth with APIs, authentication and data-exchange patterns, and the ability to scope, spec and validate integrations through sandboxes and proof-of-concept builds.
  • Joint go-to-market execution - experience developing co-sell, co-build and co-deliver plans, aligning internal and partner teams, facilitating sales enablement and creating the collateral that makes joint solutions land.
  • Executive-level relationship management - comfort owning senior stakeholder relationships across partner organisations, running structured business reviews (QBRs), and resolving conflict constructively when internal and partner priorities clash.
  • Data-driven partner management, with the habit of defining, tracking and analysing partnership KPIs and leading indicators of partner health and acting on them before issues escalate.

You may also have:

  • Experience with cloud marketplaces (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud) or OEM / embedded partnership motions.
  • Experience structuring and negotiating complex commercial and technical agreements alongside legal teams.
  • Familiarity with tiered partner certification programmes.
  • Experience or familiarity with scientific software, life sciences, pharmaceuticals, biotechnology or research-focused technology, including scientific data platforms, laboratory systems or R&D workflows. Experience in another domain-deep industry, such as Oil & Gas or Consumer Packaged Goods (CPG), would also be valuable.

Research shows us the confidence gap and imposter syndrome can get in the way of meeting outstanding candidates, so please don’t hesitate to apply — we’d love to hear from you.

By submitting your application, you agree that Dotmatics may collect your personal data for recruiting, global organization planning, and related purposes. Dotmatics Privacy Notice explains what personal information we may process, where we may process your personal information, our purposes for processing your personal information, and the rights you can exercise over Dotmatics use of your personal information. 

Dotmatics is an equal opportunity employer. We are a welcoming place for everyone, and we do our best to make sure all people feel supported and connected at work.

We Breathe Life Into Data

At Komodo Health, our mission is to reduce the global burden of disease. And we believe that smarter use of data is essential to this mission. That’s why we built the Healthcare Map — the industry’s largest, most complete, precise view of the U.S. healthcare system — by combining de-identified, real-world patient data with innovative algorithms and decades of clinical experience. The Healthcare Map serves as our foundation for a powerful suite of software applications, helping us answer healthcare’s most complex questions for our partners. Across the healthcare ecosystem, we’re helping our clients unlock critical insights to track detailed patient behaviors and treatment patterns, identify gaps in care, address unmet patient needs, and reduce the global burden of disease. 

As we pursue these goals, it remains essential to us that we stay grounded in our values: be awesome, seek growth, deliver “wow,” and enjoy the ride. At Komodo, you will be joining a team of ambitious, supportive Dragons with diverse backgrounds but a shared passion to deliver on our mission to reduce the burden of disease — and enjoy the journey along the way.

The Opportunity at Komodo Health

This role performs configuration tasks to meet Komodo Health customer requirements, working closely with the Solution Architect. They are the experts on configuration and collaborate with the project team and our clients.

This person is part of the Configuration Team, working closely with the Solution Architects to design and build out the configuration creatively and efficiently to meet the requirements. They will also work closely with the Business Analyst during the test writing phase and with the testing team during test execution to provide expertise and guidance.

Looking back on your first 12 months at Komodo Health, you will have…

  • Lead and/or contribute to the configuration of solutions for multiple customer projects, both small and large, delivering on customer requirements and enhancing customer satisfaction.
  • Participate in client-facing design reviews, working sessions, and training to demo and illustrate solutions.
  • Collaborate with other project team members to gain efficiencies and help implement best practices for project delivery and knowledge transfer.

You will accomplish these outcomes through the following responsibilities…

  • Design and configure appropriate solutions given the clients’ requirements (40%)
  • Document and implement configuration changes and data-mapping requirements (10%)
  • Review requirements and ensure solutions meet the requirements (10%)
  • Configure client-facing solutions, including structural and functional applications, troubleshooting errors, manipulating data, and transformations, all the while utilizing new and familiar tools throughout (20%)
  • Support and participate in client presentations and design reviews to build strong working relationships with clients and analyze feedback to ensure alignment (10%)
  • Participate in client training and other implementation initiatives as a part of overall project deliverables (10%)

What you bring to Komodo Health:

  • Experience configuring and solutioning on the Salesforce platforms with exposure to end-to-end project implementation lifecycles
  • Ability to effectively design scalable solutions to meet client business needs and perform system configuration 
  • Experience working in a collaborative project team environment
  • Experience authoring requirements, writing design documentation, and other related project and system documentation
  • Demonstrated analytical skills, problem-solving, and experience across the complete lifecycle of complex enterprise projects, from pre-sales, requirements gathering, design and build, review and refine, validation, and deploy 
  • Goal-oriented with a superior work ethic while being self-motivated
  • Ability to leverage AI tools (Gemini, ChatGPT, Cursor, etc.) to enhance personal productivity, streamline workflows, or improve decision-making

Additional skills and experience we’d prioritize (nice to have)…

  • Salesforce Certification and consulting experience a plus
  • Life Sciences experience, particularly Pharmaceutical is a plus
  • Experience interacting with, managing, or building with AI agentic workflows

Komodo's AI Standard

At Komodo, we're not just witnessing the AI revolution – we're leading it. This is a pivotal moment in time, where being first to market with AI transforms industries and sets the bar. We've already established industry leadership in leveraging AI to revolutionize healthcare, and we expect every team member to contribute. AI here isn't optional; it's foundational. We expect you to integrate AI into your daily work – from summarizing documents to automating workflows and uncovering insights. This isn't just about efficiency; it's about making every moment more meaningful, building on trust in AI, and driving our collective success.

Join us in shaping the future of healthcare intelligence.

Where You’ll Work

Komodo Health has a hybrid work model with hubs in San Francisco, New York City, and Chicago. Roles vary — some can be performed from anywhere in the country, others are scoped to a specific region, and some are based near one of our hubs. For hub-based Dragons, we're building intentional in-office rhythms alongside the flexibility that's core to how we work. Whatever your setup, expectations will always be clear before you join.

Clinical Field Specialist (CFS) – Women’s Health

Territory: West Texas (Covering Lubbock, Midland, Odessa, Amarillo, Abilene, San Angelo, and El Paso)

Position Summary The Clinical Field Specialist (CFS) will drive revenue growth and market expansion across the West Texas territory through direct engagement with individual Maternal-Fetal Medicine specialists (MFMs), OB/GYNs, and Genetic Counselors. This role focuses on building and maintaining strong clinical relationships while developing and executing strategic business plans that accelerate adoption. The CFS will support both established and newly launched diagnostic products, providing clinical expertise, educational support, and hands-on training in technical product applications.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Revenue & Market Growth: Increase revenue and drive market development through direct consultative sales to individual MFMs, OB/GYNs, and Genetic Counselors across the West Texas region.
  • Relationship Management: Execute effective prospecting strategies while cultivating and maintaining long-term relationships with key clinical stakeholders and decision-makers.
  • Strategic Territory Execution: Create and implement a comprehensive business plan to rapidly grow market share and revenue across a geographically expansive territory.
  • Product Launch & Support: Champion both currently marketed diagnostic assays and new product launches, serving as a clinical and technical resource for accounts.
  • Organizational Impact: Play a critical role in regional and national commercial success by sharing market insights and collaborating cross-functionally.
  • Compliance & Data Security: Work regularly with Protected Health Information (PHI) in both paper and electronic formats, utilizing secure technologies to perform daily job functions.
  • Training Requirements: Complete mandatory training relating to HIPAA/PHI privacy, General Policies and Procedure Compliance, and security within the first 30 days of hire, and maintain current status on all ongoing Natera training requirements.

Qualifications

  • Education: Bachelor’s degree required; preferred fields include Science, Nursing (RN/NP), or a related healthcare discipline.
  • Experience & Clinical Background: Three (3) years of physician sales experience in the diagnostic laboratory or women's health industry is preferred, though not strictly required for candidates with strong clinical credentials. We are actively open to Nurse Practitioners (NPs) currently working within an MFM or OB/GYN practice looking to transition into a commercial clinical specialist role.
  • Local Ties: Must reside within the West Texas territory; candidates with established roots, local familiarity, and existing clinical relationships in the region are strongly preferred.
  • Market Knowledge: Deep understanding of the OB/GYN and MFM workflow and clinical landscape, with a proven ability to build trust with providers.
  • Launch & Growth Mindset: Demonstrated ability to drive adoption, educate clinical teams, and grow volume in developing or expansive markets.
  • Technical Proficiency: Proficient with Microsoft PowerPoint, Excel, Gmail, and Salesforce.com.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Communication: Strong organizational and presentation skills with the proven ability to communicate complex clinical data effectively to diverse audiences.
  • Territory & Time Management: Exceptional time management and travel-planning skills with the ability to assess, route, and prioritize opportunities effectively across a wide geographic footprint.
  • Strategic Mindset: Adaptable, self-motivated, and results-driven, combining strong interpersonal and analytical skills with the ability to think strategically while executing tactically.

  • Consultative Problem-Solving: Assesses the operational and clinical needs of medical professionals through consultative sales, logistical coordination, and proactive problem-solving.

It combines a base salary with commissions and serves as an estimated figure rather than a guaranteed amount, providing a guideline based on average performance outcomes.

title: Retention and Growth Project & AI Coordinator (f/m/d)
description:
Purpose of Position

Our Retention & Growth Team is responsible for two keys areas;

  1. Customer Retention – ensuring long-term continuity and sustainability of our customer base. 
  2. Portfolio Growth – expanding revenue in line with Gross Profit (GP) and Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) targets.

This team leads the migration of customers onto new MarTech commercial models and updated contracts as part of the company’s wider business transformation.

In parallel, the team drives revenue optimisation by:

  • Upselling customers to higher-value Platform Offers or Service Packages
  • Cross-selling additional services or add-ons
  • Expanding existing customers into new markets or programmes
  • Downgrading customers to more suitable Platform Offers or Service Packages where appropriate

The R&G Project & AI Coordinator is an assistant-level role responsible for providing operational, contractual and project support to the Retention & Growth Team. 

A key focus of the position will be supporting contract reconciliation and contract management activities, ensuring that customer agreements, Salesforce records, internal approvals and supporting documentation are complete, accurate and aligned.

The role will also support the team in identifying and implementing AI-based efficiencies. This may include improving administrative processes, supporting AI initiatives, testing new ways of working and identifying opportunities to reduce manual effort across contract management, reporting, account preparation and other R&G activities.

Where appropriate, the R&G Project & AI Coordinator may attend customer calls and support commercial or contractual discussions. This will initially be alongside an R&G Manager or the R&G Team Leader, with the opportunity to take greater ownership of suitable activities as their knowledge and confidence develop.

This is a temporary maternity leave cover position. The role is intended to provide flexible support across the R&G Team, with priorities determined by current workload, team capacity and business requirements.
The position reports directly to the local R&G Team Leader, who will provide day-to-day management, training and prioritisation. The role will work closely with R&G Managers and relevant teams across Client Services, Legal, Finance, Global Business Operations, Go-to-Market, InfoSec and Technology.


Key Responsibilities:

  • Support the reconciliation of existing customer contracts against Salesforce records, pricing information, programme configurations and internal documentation.
  • Review contract records to identify missing agreements, amendments, approvals, signatures or supporting documentation.
  • Assist with the preparation, processing and administration of opportunities, contracts, renewals, renegotiations, upgrades, downgrades and other contractual documentation.
  • Support the identification of activities that could be simplified, accelerated or improved through AI, automation or better use of existing systems.
  • Work with the R&G Team to understand time-consuming or repetitive processes and help develop more efficient ways of completing them.
  • Support the planning and delivery of R&G projects and operational initiatives.
  • Attend customer calls where appropriate to support R&G Managers with contract, renewal or account-related discussions.
  • Support straightforward customer communications and follow-ups under the guidance of an R&G Manager or the R&G Team Leader.
  • Communicate professionally and clearly with customers and internal stakeholders.
  • Provide flexible support across the wider R&G function based on changing team priorities and capacity.


Skills & Expertise

  • Provide flexible support across the wider R&G function based on changing team priorities and capacity.
  • An interest in AI, automation and process improvement, with a willingness to test and adopt new ways of working.
  • Ability to identify repetitive or inefficient processes and suggest practical improvements
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Experience using Salesforce to manage customer communications and records.
  • Comfortable engaging with internal stakeholders and participating in customer conversations where appropriate.
  • Commercial awareness and an interest in developing knowledge of customer contracts, negotiations and retention
  • Good problem-solving skills and the confidence to highlight issues or inconsistencies.
  • Able to work independently while recognising when support or escalation is required.
  • A collaborative and flexible approach, with a willingness to support different priorities across the team.
  • Affiliate marketing experience is beneficial but not essential.

As an assistant-level position, the R&G Project & AI Coordinator will not initially have independent ownership of complex negotiations, high-risk contractual decisions or material commercial approvals.
Such matters should remain with the relevant R&G Manager, R&G Team Leader, Legal or authorised approver. Responsibility may be expanded gradually for suitable activities based on experience, training and business need.

title: Order Resolution Program Manager
description:
Positition:

The Order Resolution Program Manager builds and leads the Order Resolution Program (ORP), a national program that helps ensure patients receive the testing their physicians have ordered. When an order encounters a barrier, such as an unreachable patient, an incorrect phone number, a patient with unanswered questions about their test, or a step that requires clinic involvement, this role makes sure the right people take the right action so care is not delayed. Many of these patients are navigating a cancer diagnosis, and the program exists to support them and the Patient Coordinators who care for them.

As the program's founding owner, the Program Manager exercises independent judgment to assess the current landscape, resolve complex cases directly, and determine what the program needs to succeed, including whether and how to expand the team. The role is hands-on by design: the Program Manager works open cases alongside Patient Coordinators to understand where and why orders stall, then uses that firsthand insight and program data to set strategy, define standards, and guide leadership decisions.

The Program Manager partners across Patient Services, Territory Managers, Clinical Oncology Specialists, Patient Coordinators, Inside Sales Managers, Regional Directors, and Operations Managers, earning alignment through expertise and sound judgment rather than direct authority.

 

Primary Responsibilities:

Program Strategy & Ownership

  • Own the Order Resolution Program end-to-end across all national regions, independently assessing the current landscape, including case volume, root causes, regional variation, and existing workflows, to determine where patient orders are most at risk of delay.
  • Develop a data-supported program roadmap and staffing recommendation for Patient Services leadership, including headcount requirements, staffing structure, timeline, and whether process or tooling solutions would better serve patients.
  • Define the program operating model, including case ownership, escalation criteria, service timelines, handoff protocols, and quality standards, and adjust it as the program matures.
  • Lead the design of the team structure, role definitions, hiring profile, onboarding, and performance expectations for future team members.

Case Resolution & Patient Care Support

  • Exercise independent judgment to evaluate open ORP cases, determine the root cause of each barrier, and develop a tailored resolution strategy that accounts for the clinical context, the patient's circumstances, and available resources.
  • Work complex and high-priority cases directly, including researching LIMS, paper orders, and patient outreach tools to locate missing or updated contact information, and decide whether a case calls for administrative resolution, clinic education or engagement, or escalation.
  • Partner with Patient Coordinators to support patient outreach, providing guidance on how to approach each case and, where appropriate, connecting with patients directly so that questions about their orders are answered and care can move forward.
  • Determine when to escalate a case to the clinic, engage the field team, or close it, and document the rationale so any subsequent owner can continue seamlessly.
  • Maintain a real-time view of all open cases, including status, owner, next action, and age, and follow up consistently to confirm actions are completed and patients are not left waiting.

Analytics & Performance Reporting

  • Design, build, and maintain the ORP reporting infrastructure, including dashboards, KPI scorecards, and regional trend analysis, and define the metrics used to measure program success.
  • Report regularly to Patient Services leadership on case volume, resolution rates, time to resolution, and order completion outcomes, translating data into clear insights about what is working, what is not, and what should change.
  • Analyze recurring barriers, such as common reasons patients cannot be reached or questions that arise repeatedly, and develop recommendations that reduce the number of patients whose orders require intervention in the first place.

Cross-Functional Leadership & Process Improvement

  • Partner with Territory Managers, Clinical Oncology Specialists, Associate Clinical Oncology Specialists, and Patient Coordinators to set clear expectations, communicate promptly, and share accountability on every open case.
  • Partner with Inside Sales Managers, Regional Directors, and Operations Managers to align program priorities, resolve regional barriers, and ensure teams understand their role in supporting patient orders.
  • Serve as the subject matter expert for ORP, providing guidance and consultation to field and operations partners and developing best practices, training, and standard work that can be adopted nationally.
  • Identify systemic process gaps and bring structured, data-backed recommendations to leadership, including changes to workflows, status definitions, tooling, and cross-team handoffs, with the patient experience as the guiding lens.
  • Performs other duties as assigned.

 

Qualifications:

 

  • Bachelor's degree in healthcare administration, business, life sciences, or a related field; or equivalent professional experience in a role requiring independent judgment, program ownership, and decision-making in a healthcare or clinical operations environment.
  • 5 or more years of experience in healthcare operations, patient services, program or project management, or a comparable environment, with demonstrated ownership of a program, workflow, or initiative from assessment through execution.
  • Demonstrated ability to assess a complex operating landscape, identify root causes, and develop and present a data-supported recommendation, including resourcing and staffing needs, to senior leadership.
  • Proven ability to independently assess multi-variable situations and determine the appropriate course of action without direct supervision, particularly in patient-facing or clinically sensitive contexts.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence and drive accountability across cross-functional teams, including field, sales, and operations leaders, without direct authority.
  • Strong analytical capability, including building performance reporting, interpreting trends, and communicating findings clearly to leadership; advanced MS Excel or equivalent skills required.
  • Experience in a call center, patient outreach, or high-volume case management environment (inbound and outbound).
  • Proficiency in CRM platforms, case tracking systems, and data tools; familiarity with skip tracing tools and LIMS is a strong plus.
  • Prior experience leading, coaching, or building a team is preferred. Background in patient coordination or another patient-facing healthcare role is strongly preferred.

 

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

Technical

  • Program and project management expertise, including scoping, planning, prioritization, milestone tracking, and stakeholder management.
  • Specialized knowledge of healthcare operations, patient services workflows, and clinical coordination sufficient to evaluate case scenarios and develop resolution strategies without relying on standardized scripts.
  • Advanced proficiency in CRM platforms, case tracking systems, and reporting tools, with the ability to design KPI dashboards that give leadership real-time visibility into program performance and patient order outcomes.
  • Strong quantitative skills, including comfort working with large data sets to identify trends, build business cases, and model staffing and capacity needs.
  • Experience with skip tracing tools and multi-database research methods, and with process documentation and standard operating procedure development.

Behavioral

  • Exercises sound, independent judgment consistently, treating each case and each program decision as a situation requiring individualized analysis.
  • Builds before being asked: sees what a new program needs, takes ownership of the decision, and moves forward without waiting to be told something is off track.
  • Balances urgency and care: moves quickly because patients are waiting, and makes thoughtful decisions because the stakes are real.
  • Thinks like a program owner and acts like a teammate: comfortable working individual cases to learn the work, and equally comfortable stepping back to set strategy and advise leadership.
  • Earns credibility with cross-functional partners through expertise, clear communication, and follow-through, and uses it to drive action across teams they do not directly control.
  • Coaches and develops others, and is ready to build and lead a team as the program grows.

 

Physical Demands & Work Environment:

  • This is a primarily remote position. Occasional on-site attendance may be required for planning sessions, leadership reviews, or business needs.
  • Duties are performed in a home office or professional office setting and require the ability to use a computer keyboard, communicate over the telephone, and read printed and digital material.
  • This role may require working outside standard business hours at times to address time-sensitive case situations or program needs.

Travel:

Minimal travel required. Occasional travel (estimated less than 15%) may be required for national leadership meetings, regional business reviews, or planning sessions.

title: Account Supervisor
description:
About Avalere Health

United by one profound purpose: to reach EVERY PATIENT POSSIBLE. At Avalere Health, we ensure every patient is identified, treated, supported, and cared for. Equally. Our Advisory, Medical, and Marketing teams come together – powerfully and intentionally – to forge unconventional connections, building a future where healthcare is not a barrier and no patient is left behind. 

Achieving our mission starts with providing enriching, purpose-driven careers for our team that empower them to make a tangible impact on patient lives. We are committed to creating a culture where our employees are empowered to bring their whole selves to work and tap into the power of diverse backgrounds and skillsets to play a part in making a difference for every patient, everywhere. 

Our flexible approach to working allows our global teams to decide where they want to work, whether in-office or at home based on team and client need. Major city hubs in London, Manchester, Washington, D.C., and New York, and smaller offices globally, serve as collaboration hubs allowing our teams to come together when it matters. Homeworkers are equally supported, with dedicated social opportunities and resources.  

Our inclusive culture is at the heart of everything we do. We proudly support our employees in bringing their whole selves to work with our six Employee Network Groups – Diverse Ability, Family, Gender, LGBTQ+, Mental Health, and Race/Ethnicity. These groups provide opportunities to promote diversity, equity, and inclusion and to connect, learn, and socialise through regular meetings and programs of activity. We are an accredited Fertility Friendly employer with our Fertility Policy, enhanced parental leave, and culture of flexibility ensuring every employee feels supported across their family planning journey and can work in a way that suits their family’s needs. 

We are deeply invested in supporting professional growth for our employees through day-to-day career experiences, access to thousands of on-demand training sessions, regular career conversations, and the opportunity for global, cross-capability career moves.  

We take pride in being part of the Disability Confident Scheme. This helps make sure you can be interviewed fairly if you have a disability, long term health condition, or are neurodiverse. If you'd like to apply and need adjustments made, you can let us know in your application.


About the role:
 
The Account Supervisor is a driven, engaged client service professional who thrives in a collaborative team atmosphere and excels at developing unique solutions that differentiate our client’s brands in the market.
 What we can offer You will receive a 401K plan with an employer match contribution up to 4% (immediately vested), as well as life insurance, disability coverage, and medical, dental, and vision plans for peace of mind. Enjoy flexible working arrangements, including hybrid and remote work, along with the option to work from anywhere across the globe two weeks each year. We provide 20 vacation days plus one personal well-being day, recognise 9 public holidays, along with gifted end-of-year holidays and an early Summer Friday finish in June, July, and August. Access free counselling through our employee assistance program and personalized health support. Our enhanced maternity, paternity, family leave, and fertility policies provide support across every stage of your family-planning journey. You can also benefit from continuous opportunities to professionally develop with on-demand training, support, and global mobility opportunities across the business. We encourage all applicants to read our candidate privacy notice before applying to Avalere Health.

We are seeking a high-energy, adaptable, and results-driven Account Sales Representative (ASR) to join our Women's Health sales team. This is an exciting opportunity for a motivated sales professional who thrives in a fast-paced, competitive environment and is eager to make a meaningful impact in women's healthcare.

As an ASR, you will partner closely with an experienced Clinical Field Specialist (CFS) to drive account growth, strengthen customer relationships, and expand adoption of Natera's Women's Health products among OB/GYNs, Maternal-Fetal Medicine (MFM) specialists, and their clinical teams.

The ideal candidate is a proactive, resourceful self-starter who learns quickly, builds trust effortlessly, and brings a strong sense of urgency to everything they do. Success in this role requires someone who can adapt to different personalities, anticipate customer needs, take initiative, and contribute to a high-performing sales partnership.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Partner with your assigned CFS to execute strategic territory plans, increase utilization within existing accounts, identify expansion opportunities, and support overall revenue growth.
  • Collaborate closely with your CFS to prioritize opportunities, coordinate customer engagement, and execute territory initiatives with speed, accountability, and a shared commitment to results.
  • Establish rapport and credibility with physicians, practice managers, medical assistants, and other clinical staff. Adapt your communication style to engage effectively with diverse personalities and decision-makers.
  • Serve as a responsive, solutions-oriented resource for customers by coordinating sample logistics, addressing account needs, troubleshooting challenges, and ensuring a seamless customer experience.
  • Strengthen relationships with established accounts, identify opportunities to increase product adoption, and support the introduction of new products and services.
  • Recognize competitive challenges, uncover unmet customer needs, and proactively implement solutions that strengthen customer loyalty and territory performance.
  • Work closely with internal Natera teams to resolve customer needs, support positive client and patient experiences, and maintain compliance with company policies and confidentiality requirements.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience required.
  • Minimum of 2 years of demonstrated success in B2B sales. Experience in medical sales, diagnostics, healthcare, or life sciences is preferred.

  • Authentic, personable communicator with the ability to establish trust, read the room, and adapt their approach to different customers and situations.
  • Thrives in a fast-moving environment, manages competing priorities effectively, and responds quickly to customer and business needs.
  • Energized by ambitious goals, comfortable overcoming objections, and persistent in pursuing growth opportunities.
  • Strong team player who values partnership, communicates proactively, and contributes to shared sales objectives.
  • Excellent time management, follow-through, and problem-solving skills. Proficiency with Salesforce.com, Gmail, Microsoft PowerPoint, and Excel preferred.

Compensation & Benefits

  • Car allowance program.
  • Restricted Stock Units (RSUs) package.
  • Opportunity to contribute to a growing Women's Health business and make a meaningful

Natera™ is a global leader in cell-free DNA (cfDNA) testing, dedicated to oncology, women’s health, and organ health. title: EH&S Lead
description:
About Arc Institute

Arc Institute is an independent nonprofit research organization at the interface of artificial intelligence and biology, working to accelerate scientific progress and understand the root causes of complex diseases. Founded in 2021 and based in Palo Alto, Arc partners with Stanford University, UC Berkeley, and UC San Francisco.

Unlike academia, our scientists have long-term funding and industry-like resources. Unlike industry, they're free to pursue high-risk, long-term research without commercial pressures. Arc's Technology Centers and Core Investigator labs work side by side, integrating experimental and computational biology under one roof to tackle problems neither could solve alone.

Our two Institute Initiatives reflect this model in action:

  • Virtual Cell Initiative: Building a full-stack virtual cell model to identify disease mechanisms and nominate drug targets,  accelerating the path from biological insight to clinical trials.
  • Alzheimer's Disease Initiative: Mapping the genes, pathways, and environmental factors behind Alzheimer's disease to develop drug candidates that address root causes.

More than 300 Arconauts work together at our Palo Alto headquarters, backed by substantial long-term philanthropic funding.

About the position

As EH&S Lead, you will own the development, implementation, and the management of Arc’s Environmental, Health, and Safety programs and culture. You will design solutions that satisfy overlapping local, state, and federal requirements, and serve as Arc’s primary point of contact for regulatory and certifying agencies.

Your remit covers chemical hygiene, biosafety, OSHA compliance, medical and hazardous waste, and Arc’s safety permits and sustainability programs. You will hire and manage a biosafety manager and direct the work of outside vendors and consultants.

About you

  • You are deeply committed to the health and safety of your colleagues, and you achieve it through partnership with the labs rather than around them.
  • You are genuinely curious about the science here and want to understand the research at a real level of depth.
  • You thrive in a diverse environment and enjoy working with scientists and students from many backgrounds.
  • You are energized by building programs and forging cross-functional partnerships that strengthen the community and the mission.

In this position you will

  • Provide safety leadership and EH&S subject matter expertise aligned with Arc’s operating principles.
  • Develop, implement, and maintain EH&S programs, procedures, and systems in compliance with federal, state, and local regulations, driving continuous improvement.
  • Develop Arc’s safety strategy and carry out safety policies and procedures in accordance with all applicable regulatory and organizational requirements.
  • Hire, manage, and develop a biosafety manager, setting clear priorities and standards for their work.
  • Advise Arc’s administrative team on safety and compliance for specific projects and operations.
  • Define Arc’s approach to  EH&S employee safety and onboarding training, with a focus on efficiency and engagement.
  • Own and evolve Arc’s compliance programs including, but not limited to, the Cal/OSHA bloodborne pathogens standard and biosafety program, chemical safety, radiation safety, and controlled substances.
  • Own Arc’s environmental compliance strategy, including the industrial wastewater discharge permit, hazardous waste requirements, and regulatory permitting.
  • Own risk assessment program and conduct regular risk assessments and safety audits to identify workplace hazards — chemical, physical, biological, industrial, and radiological among them — and remediate hazards or recommend improvements to reduce them.
  • Lead investigations of accidents, incidents, injuries, and complaints concerning potential hazards or unsafe conditions to determine root causes and preventive measures.
  • Conduct safety inspections and walkthroughs that deliver meaningful insight and surface continuous improvement opportunities across Arc’s labs.
  • Develop and manage EH&S management systems covering chemical inventories, SDS, near-miss reporting, permitting compliance, and incident investigations.
  • Oversee regulated medical and hazardous waste programs, including vendor contracting.
  • Act as primary point of contact for regulatory and certifying agencies and government authorities.
  • Own procurement and maintenance of safety equipment and supply inventory, ensuring onsite personnel are adequately protected from workplace hazards.
  • Respond to emergency situations involving hazardous materials.
  • Develop, own and maintain Arc’s EH&S wiki.

Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in industrial hygiene, biology, chemistry, environmental science, occupational safety and health, or a related field, or equivalent experience. Master’s degree preferred.
  • 8+ years of laboratory experience, including 5 years in EH&S, with a minimum of 2 years leading and developing EH&S programs.
  • Highly organized and detail-oriented, with a track record of managing multiple projects accurately and on time.
  • Working knowledge of the scientific and technical aspects of applicable regulations — including Cal/OSHA, CalEPA, the Medical Waste Management Act, EPA, DEA, OSHA, NRC, and NFPA — and how they bear on laboratory operations.
  • Strong interpersonal skills, with a demonstrated ability to prioritize resources, influence group behavior, and build consensus around safety practice.
  • Able to work independently and as part of a dynamic team, with a positive attitude, a strong sense of urgency, and a bias toward action.
  • Interest in learning new techniques, keeping accurate records, and working within established policies.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience managing people, including hiring, coaching, and developing direct reports.
  • Demonstrated success leading change management in a research or lab environment.
  • Experience with Animal Research Occupational Health and Safety programs.
  • Experience supporting laboratory animal research involving biohazardous or hazardous materials.
  • Associate Safety Professional (ASP), Certified Safety Professional (CSP), or Certified Industrial Hygienist (CIH) certification.

The base salary range for this position is $127,000 to $157,000. These amounts reflect the range of base salary that the Institute reasonably would expect to pay a new hire or internal candidate for this position. The actual base compensation paid to any individual for this position may vary depending on factors such as experience, market conditions, education/training, skill level, and whether the compensation is internally equitable, and does not include bonuses, commissions, differential pay, other forms of compensation, or benefits. This position is also eligible to receive an annual discretionary bonus, with the amount dependent on individual and institute performance factors.

title: Building Engineer
description:
About Arc Institute

Arc Institute is an independent nonprofit research organization at the interface of artificial intelligence and biology, working to accelerate scientific progress and understand the root causes of complex diseases. Founded in 2021 and based in Palo Alto, Arc partners with Stanford University, UC Berkeley, and UC San Francisco.

Unlike academia, our scientists have long-term funding and industry-like resources. Unlike industry, they're free to pursue high-risk, long-term research without commercial pressures. Arc's Technology Centers and Core Investigator labs work side by side, integrating experimental and computational biology under one roof to tackle problems neither could solve alone.

Our two Institute Initiatives reflect this model in action:

  • Virtual Cell Initiative: Building a full-stack virtual cell model to identify disease mechanisms and nominate drug targets,  accelerating the path from biological insight to clinical trials.
  • Alzheimer's Disease Initiative: Mapping the genes, pathways, and environmental factors behind Alzheimer's disease to develop drug candidates that address root causes.

More than 300 Arconauts work together at our Palo Alto headquarters, backed by substantial long-term philanthropic funding.

About the position

Arc Institute operates advanced wet-lab and research facilities where uptime directly protects irreplaceable science: cell lines, samples, and instruments representing years of work. We're hiring a hands-on Facilities Building Engineer to own the reliability of our building systems and lab-critical environments. 

This is a working engineer role. You will diagnose and fix problems yourself, and you’ll know when a job calls for a specialist. You will direct our vendor and contract-support partners to get it done right, on time, and on budget. You'll also run facility projects end-to-end and serve as the calm, service-oriented point of contact for the researchers who depend on the building.

About you

  • You catch problems early, before they turn into a researcher’s bad day. You’re just as comfortable running a diagnostic yourself as you are getting a vendor on the phone to handle something that’s not yours to touch. You want to know why a system works the way it does, not just how to patch it.
  • You like being around science, even though you’re not a scientist. You get that a freezer failure here isn’t an inconvenience; it’s years of someone’s work. That weight doesn’t stress you out. It’s part of what makes the job worth doing well.
  • You don’t need a lot of ramp-up time or close supervision to take ownership. You’re comfortable being the primary engineer onsite, you set your own priorities, and you integrate with the team from day one.
  • You’re straightforward and easy to track down. You build trust through consistent follow-through.

 

In this position you will

  • Serve as the primary onsite contact for facilities service requests; deliver responsive, professional service to researchers and staff.
  • Operate and maintain lab HVAC systems serving wet labs — air-change rates, pressure cascades/room differentials, VAV/reheat, fume-hood and BSC exhaust — and respond to alarms before they threaten research.
  • Support lab utilities: RO/DI and lab-water loops, lab gases (CO₂, N₂, compressed air, vacuum), acid-neutralization systems, eyewash/safety-shower testing.
  • Coordinate biosafety-adjacent equipment maintenance (fume-hood face-velocity checks, BSC recertification) with EH&S (Environmental Health & Safety).
  • Self-perform routine multi-trade work (HVAC/mechanical troubleshooting, plumbing, electrical, and general building repairs) within your qualifications and licensing
  • Interpret and adjust the building automation system (e.g., Alerton, Automated Logic, Johnson Controls, Siemens)
  • Exercise sound judgment on when to self-perform vs. engage a specialist
  • Maintain standby-power readiness: generator, ATS, and UPS testing supporting freezers and critical loads.
  • Run small-to-mid facility projects (renovations, equipment installs, system upgrades): scope, budget, contractor coordination, and closeout.
  • Support compliance with Cal/OSHA requirements (IIPP, LOTO, confined space, hot work), NFPA 70E, fire and life-safety codes and testing, California building, mechanical, plumbing, and electrical codes, and Title 24
  • Support compliance with Bay Area Air Quality Management District (BAAQMD) permits for generators and boilers, and with CUPA, hazardous materials, and wastewater-discharge requirements
  • Align building operations with CDC/NIH BMBL biosafety guidance in coordination with EH&S.
  • Drive energy efficiency and monitoring across high-load systems (compute/cooling, freezer farm), identifying sustainability and cost-reduction opportunities.

Requirements

  • 5+ years operating and maintaining building mechanical systems in a life-sciences, commercial, or institutional facility, including direct HVAC troubleshooting experience
  • Demonstrated ability to self-perform routine work across mechanical/HVAC (deep expertise), plumbing, electrical, and general construction, with sound judgment on when to escalate specialized work to vendors
  • Proven ability to direct and manage the quality of vendors and contract support
  • Ability to read mechanical, electrical, and plumbing (MEP) drawings; proficiency with BMS/BAS and CMMS software
  • EPA 608 Universal refrigerant certification
  • Valid California driver's license
  • Willingness to participate in a shared after-hours on-call rotation for lab-critical systems, including responding onsite when needed
  • Ability to lift up to 50 lbs

Preferred Qualifications

  • Degree in Mechanical or Electrical Engineering preferred; equivalent hands-on experience may be substituted
  • Experience in a BSL-2 research or vivarium environment
  • Journey-level trade credential or Stationary Engineer certification (e.g., IUOE/Stationary Engineers Local 39)
  • OSHA 30, boiler operator, or backflow tester certification
  • Experience with -80°C freezer farms and cryogenic systems
  • Experience supporting asset-replacement and capital-planning processes
  • Bilingual in English and Spanish, to support coordination with trades and vendor teams

This position is also eligible to receive an annual discretionary bonus, with the amount dependent on individual and institute performance factors.

title: Literacy Coach
description:
About the Team

Michigan Online School (MOS) is a K-12 tuition-free online public school in the state of Michigan. At MOS, we empower students to be their best by enabling them to learn in ways that are right for them – using innovative technology at home, at their proper level, and at their own pace.

The Literacy Coach partners with teachers, school leaders, and instructional teams to strengthen literacy instruction and improve student achievement. Through job-embedded coaching, professional learning, collaborative planning, classroom modeling, and data-informed support, the Literacy Coach helps educators implement evidence-based literacy practices aligned with Michigan academic standards and state literacy initiatives.

The Literacy Coach works collaboratively with teachers, principals, leadership teams, and data specialists to build instructional capacity, support effective literacy interventions, strengthen reading outcomes, and promote continuous school improvement. This position emphasizes a collaborative, relationship-driven approach to professional growth and instructional excellence.

Eligibility: Open to residents of Michigan

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

Instructional Coaching & Teacher Support

  • Build and maintain strong, collaborative relationships with teaching staff grounded in mutual respect, teamwork, and accountability.

  • Partner with classroom teachers to implement evidence-based early literacy instructional practices through job-embedded coaching.

  • Provide individualized and small-group coaching through classroom observations, instructional modeling, co-teaching, collaborative planning, goal-setting, and reflective conversations.

  • Model effective whole-group and small-group literacy instruction for teachers and students.

  • Support teachers in developing effective classroom literacy environments and implementing research-based instructional strategies and literacy programs.

  • Coach teachers in structured literacy lesson design and the implementation of practices aligned with state standards.

  • Provide ongoing feedback to help teachers reflect on, establish goals, practice, and refine instructional skills aligned with the Essential Instructional Practices in Literacy.

Data Analysis & Student Achievement

  • Analyze formative assessment, screening, and diagnostic data to develop and inform instructional plans.

  • Support teachers in collecting, analyzing, and using student data to guide instructional decisions and improve learning outcomes.

  • Administer and interpret universal screeners to identify students with characteristics of dyslexia.

  • Train and support teachers in identifying reading deficiencies and implementing appropriate evidence-based interventions.

  • Support the identification and implementation of instructional strategies to address students' individual literacy needs.

Professional Learning & School Leadership

  • Lead, organize, and facilitate professional learning communities (PLCs) and collaborative professional development opportunities for teachers.

  • Facilitate the school's literacy leadership committee and support the development of a comprehensive literacy continuum.

  • Assist building principals in identifying instructional strengths and areas of need related to literacy instruction.

  • Communicate student progress, instructional needs, and coaching outcomes with principals and school leadership teams.

  • Attend required coaching trainings, networking sessions, and professional learning opportunities.

  • Engage in continuous professional learning to remain current on research-supported literacy instruction, coaching practices, and the science of reading.

Required Qualifications & Experience

  • Valid Michigan teaching certificate.

  • Five or more years of successful teaching experience; virtual teaching experience preferred.

  • Experience facilitating professional learning at the grade-level or team level.

  • Demonstrated experience supporting students with dyslexia or characteristics of dyslexia, including the implementation of evidence-based reading interventions.

  • Training or certification in a dyslexia-focused instructional program.

  • Strong knowledge of reading and writing development, literacy acquisition, and evidence-based instructional practices.

  • Familiarity with Michigan's Dyslexia Handbook and state requirements related to early screening and intervention.

  • Knowledge of current Michigan literacy standards and legislation, including Public Acts 146 and 147.

  • Experience using formative assessments, universal screeners, and diagnostic assessment tools to inform instructional planning.

  • Ability to use classroom observation data and formative assessment practices to guide instructional coaching and professional learning.

  • Proficiency with technology-based instructional and organizational tools.

  • Demonstrated ability to build positive professional relationships and collaborate effectively with teachers, administrators, and other stakeholders.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Master's degree in Literacy or a related field, or Reading Specialist certification.

  • LETRS training or equivalent professional learning focused on research-based early literacy practices and the science of reading.

  • Additional training or certification in evidence-based structured literacy instruction.

title: Clinical Laboratory Scientist II
description:
Location: On-Site in Boulder, CO (Foresight Dx business unit, a Natera company)

Shift: Tuesday - Saturday, 11:30am-8:00pm

About our Company:

Foresight Diagnostics is a molecular diagnostics company pioneering non-invasive cancer detection through highly sensitive, cell-free DNA-based liquid biopsy technologies. Our proprietary methods - originally developed at Stanford University - are designed to detect smaller tumors earlier and enable more personalized treatment strategies for patients with cancer. 

We sit at the intersection of molecular biology, bioinformatics, and next-generation sequencing (NGS), and we translate rigorous science into clinically meaningful solutions. Following our acquisition by Natera, we now combine the agility of a mission-driven startup with the scale and resources of a global leader in cell-free DNA testing. It’s an exciting moment to join us. 

Headquartered in Boulder, Colorado, our team operates in a high accountability, collaborative environment where quality and continuous improvement aren’t just values - they’re how we work every day.

About the Role

The Clinical Laboratory Scientist II will be responsible for performing a variety of laboratory procedures involved in end-to-end processing of biological samples to enable successful downstream next-generation sequencing (NGS). Processing will include accessioning and both manual and automated extraction, library preparation, hybrid capture, sequencing and QC steps. Under the guidance of the Director of Clinical Laboratory Operations and the Laboratory Director, you will work collaboratively within the clinical laboratory leveraging your technical knowledge, skills and abilities to ensure efficient and quality results are provided to our clients and patients while also informing/participating in process improvements. This position will report to the Lab Manager.

 

What You Will Bring

  • Bachelor’s or Master's degree in chemical, physical, biological, or clinical laboratory science or medical technology from an accredited institution

    • Education received at a college or university located outside of the United States or United States Territories requires a credentials equivalency evaluation by an approved agency

  • Hold a current and active American Society of Clinical Pathology (ASCP) board certification

  • Hold current and valid Clinical Laboratory Scientist licensure (Generalist or CGMBS)

  • Demonstrate a working knowledge of the general biological principles that govern DNA biology

  • Possess a strong foundational understanding of common molecular biology techniques, such as PCR/qPCR, DNA ligation, and DNA extraction

  • Working level knowledge or ability to learn use of common molecular biology instruments; Agilent Tapestation/capillary electrophoresis, Qubit, plate readers, thermocyclers and other common laboratory instruments

  • Previous experience handling human biological materials is required

  • Working knowledge of how to safely operate in a BSL-2 environment is required

  • Previous experience handling, processing, and extracting DNA from biological specimens is required

 

What You Will Do

Technical

  • Perform routine and complex diagnostic laboratory testing on patient samples for clinical, biopharma, and academic partnerships.

  • Provide technical guidance and oversight to non-licensed personnel for pre-analytical, analytical and post-analytical activities.

  • Interpret data and results of all analyses according to set procedures and guidelines.

  • Support day to day operations by assisting with data entry, receiving samples and consumables, reagent preparation, sample preparation, temperature recording, laboratory maintenance and documentation.

  • Identify and resolve problems that may adversely affect test performance or reporting of test results following the escalation path to clinical leadership as needed.

  • Assist with research, translational research, regulated products through the execution of partnership studies and internal/external validation studies.

  • Participate as a contributing member of the clinical laboratory by assisting in routine activities, to include but not limited to general upkeep and stocking, SOP author and review, and continuous improvement.

  • Proposes assay and process improvements and conducts improvement activities under guidance.

  • Demonstrate forward thinking and initiative in work planning and execution of work in order to achieve on-time report delivery.

  • Participate in new or revised assay launches giving input on launch logistics as appropriate.

  • Participate in work planning initiatives and scheduling.

Quality, Training & Equipment

  • Maintaining documentation in compliance with Good Laboratory Practices and Quality Systems.

  • Assist with quality control and quality assurance activities. Responsible for reviewing and analyzing the health of laboratory quality metrics in collaboration with clinical leadership.

  • Complete initial training and maintain competencies as current and up to date for all trained assays.

  • Wear appropriate PPE as required and comply with safety rules and regulations.

  • Follow standard operating procedures (SOP).

  • Participate in IQ/OQ/PQ for equipment to ensure ability to train team members on proper use and maintenance as appropriate.

  • Escalate equipment issues that impact TAT or patient safety.

  • Assist, perform, and review instrument correlation studies. Collaborate with operational leadership on equipment analysis for assay expansion or improvement.

  • Perform instrument and procedural calibrations and maintenance.

  • Advises and drives progress on troubleshooting equipment issues.

  • Adhere to the laboratory's quality control policies including document control activities, change management, corrective preventative action.

  • May act as trainer in place of designated trainer/training team.

Team

  • Cultivate, build and maintain positive and collaborative relationships within teams and cross-functionally.

  • Operate as a thought leader and hold cross-functional teams accountable to regulatory, quality, scientific and performance standards to ensure the highest quality for sample integrity.

  • Seen as a role model for safety behavior standards and cultural tenets.

  • Serves as a leader from the bench, demonstrating consistency in good lab practices.

 

Working Conditions and Physical Effort

Staff in this role must be able to perform the essential functions of the job with or without a reasonable accommodation. This position is also eligible for additional compensation and benefits through Natera’s robust Total Rewards program, including:

  • Annual performance incentive bonus
  • Long-term equity awards

  • 401(k) with company match

The Natera team consists of highly dedicated statisticians, geneticists, doctors, laboratory scientists, business professionals, software engineers and many other professionals from world-class institutions, who care deeply for our work and each other. title: Scientist II, Screening
description:
Profluent is the frontier AI lab for biology. Profluent builds powerful foundation models for all of life's molecules, unlocking solutions that transform medicine, agriculture, and beyond. Founded in 2022 and headquartered in Emeryville, CA, Profluent is backed by leading investors including Altimeter Capital, Bezos Expeditions, Spark Capital, Insight Partners, Air Street Capital, AIX Ventures, and Convergent Ventures and has raised over $150M to date.

The Role

Profluent is seeking a motivated, rigorous, and collaborative scientist to establish and lead a centralized gene editor screening function. High-quality experimental data is a core input to our protein design models, and this role will own the screening operations that produce it.

This role centers on building and running a screening core responsible for assay standardization, data quality, and team development. At first, you will support campaigns that generate training and evaluation data for our protein design models, and the scope may grow to cover more programs. You will design, run, and troubleshoot mammalian genome editing assays with NGS readouts in arrayed and pooled formats. You will set the technical standards that make our data reproducible and trustworthy. You will also build and mentor a team of Research Associates, and coordinate closely with Automation, Bioinformatics, Data Science, and Biology to keep the screening pipeline running smoothly from start to finish.

As a leader of the team, you will balance hands-on scientific execution with people management and process development. You will identify, prioritize, and drive infrastructure projects that improve throughput, consistency, and assay sensitivity. You will also work with leadership to shape the long-term scope of the core.

We welcome candidates from diverse backgrounds who share our commitment to revolutionizing biology, driving meaningful innovation, and making a lasting impact on global healthcare.

This role offers a unique opportunity to shape the future of AI-driven protein design while collaborating with a dynamic, interdisciplinary team of experts in machine learning, protein engineering, cell biology, and gene editing.

 

Responsibilities

Team Leadership

  • Build and lead a team of 2–4 Research Associates, including hiring, training, performance management, and career development
  • Train and mentor staff on aseptic technique, assay execution, and documentation standards
  • Foster a supportive team culture that prioritizes growth, engagement, and well-being

Execution

  • Prioritize, schedule, and resource cross-functional experiments in coordination with Automation and Bioinformatics
  • Design, execute, troubleshoot, and analyze mammalian genome editing assays with NGS readouts in arrayed and pooled formats
  • Onboard new assays and extend existing assays to new enzyme classes
  • Maintain sample chain of custody from plate mapping through automation, sample preparation, and sequencing submission, partnering with Bioinformatics on data schema and capture
  • Communicate technical results clearly to both expert and non-expert audiences
  • Deliver QC'd, analysis-ready datasets with documented QC flags to ML

Process Development

  • Define and enforce technical standards, and write and maintain SOPs
  • Qualify new assays and define acceptance criteria based on reproducibility data
  • Maintain cell line quality and inventory for screening assays, in coordination with teams that manage cell banks
  • Characterize assay sensitivity, including the minimum detectable difference in activity at standard replicate counts
  • Identify, prioritize, and plan infrastructure projects that continually improve assays and processes
  • Coordinate process development across Automation, Bioinformatics, Data Science, and Biology
  • Evaluate the costs and benefits of centralizing high-throughput workflows in partnership with other teams
  • Work with leadership to assess and refine the scope of core functions

 

Qualifications

  • PhD in Molecular Biology, Biochemistry, Cell Biology, or a related field and 2+ years of relevant industry experience, or MS in a related field and 10+ years of relevant industry experience
  • Hands-on experience with bacterial and mammalian cell culture, genome editing, and NGS-based assays
  • Experience with high-throughput experimentation and analysis of large datasets
  • Experience with LIMS or ELN systems for sample and experiment tracking
  • Demonstrated ability to establish technical standards and drive consistent execution across operators


Preferences

  • Experience working in or building a core facility or centralized service function
  • Track record of building or improving high-throughput processes
  • Experience leading infrastructure or process improvement projects
  • Experience with liquid handling automation and tech transfer
  • Experience with cell bank and inventory management
  • Strong foundation in experimental design and statistics, including power analysis and design of experiments (DOE)

$144,000—$160,000 USD
